segment_summary: এখানে খাদ্যকে কেবল শারীরিক পুষ্টির উৎস হিসেবে না দেখে, আত্মার গভীরে ভাজা থাকা একটি জীবন্ত আর্কাইভ হিসেবে চিত্রিত করা হয়।

segment_enrichment.angle: Framing the 'taste' as a fugitive particle—a physical ghost that momentarily adheres to the tongue before scattering into memory dust.
segment_enrichment.story_option: Setting: Beside a worn, open travel folder containing unused spice packets (cold/dry); Desire: To coax the volatile aroma from these inert containers back into vibrant reality; Obstacle: The dryness and foreign climate leeches all vitality from the spices; Turn: A sudden gust of wind brings a single, phantom scent of wet earth.
segment_enrichment.subject_rotation: Interrogating the role of language itself: how does naming (Samosa) fundamentally corrupt the sensory experience of the original (Singara)?
segment_enrichment.sensory_detail: Smell: The phantom scent of dry earth mixed with frying fat clinging to unused linen.
segment_enrichment.research_question: What specific vocabulary in Bengali suggests an intangible residue—something lingering without form (a poetic equivalent for a flavor ghost)?
segment_enrichment.structural_variant: A segmented structure that builds tension by withholding a single decisive concluding phrase until the very last line.
segment_enrichment.variety_note: Unlike neighbouring chapters that dwell on external market scenes or tangible texture, this chapter moves entirely inward, focusing on the subtle, unresolved vibrational echo of the flavor in memory itself.
